title: Legacy metadata mapping playbook (scratch)
content:
Context:
This is a messy scratchpad capturing heuristics for mapping old/legacy metadata fields into the new canonical label schema. We have ~2.3M rows from product telemetry and partner imports with inconsistent field names, nested JSON blobs, and a mix of human-edits + automated tags. Primary goal: produce high-precision mappings for downstream training and audits with a clear audit trail (mapping rule id, confidence, sample examples).

Notes on current problem space:
- multiple legacy keys that mean the same thing: src, source_system, ingestion_source, originator
- boolean-ish fields stored as strings: "True", "0", "t", "false", "yes/no", empty string
- historical label values that have typos or old spellings: "custmer", "cust", "customer"
- structured tags stored in a freeform text field (comma separated, semicolon; nested with brackets)
- some rows include embedded JSON in a text column (e.g., metadata_blob = '{"env":"prod","owner":"eng-ops"}')

Quick principles (draft):
1) Prefer deterministic high-precision rules first (regex + normalization).
2) Where deterministic rules cannot confidently map, route to small human review sample or produce an "unknown_legacy" bucket with tracing.
3) Keep the original raw value in an audit column for all transformed rows.
4) Assign confidence: HIGH if normalized via whitelist OR exact match mapping; MEDIUM if fuzzy normalized (edit distance <= 2) + heuristic; LOW if only inferred by co-occurrence.
5) Log rule id that produced mapping for downstream debugging.

Candidate normalized pipeline (stages):
- stage 0: raw extraction (keep raw_value)
- stage 1: whitespace trim + unicode normalize + collapse repeated punctuation
- stage 2: tokenization for multi-tag fields (split on , ; | / \n  and ignore brackets/quotes)
- stage 3: canonicalization table lookups (customer->customer, cust->customer)
- stage 4: regex-based parsing (extract numeric ids, email domains, env tags)
- stage 5: fallback fuzzy-match via small lookup lists (n-grams + frequency threshold)

Examples and thinking-through (very important for audits):
- input: src = "prod_api_v2" -> rule: regex /prod(_|-)api/ -> mapped_source: "production_api" confidence: HIGH rule_id: src_regex_01
- input: source_system = "SAP_System-12" -> regex extract /SAP/i -> mapped_source: "sap" confidence: MEDIUM rule_id: src_regex_02 notes: check if SAP vs S4H mismatch in corpus
- input: ingestion_source = "" (empty) but metadata_blob contains '"ingested_by":"partner-x"' -> mapped_source: "partner-x" confidence: HIGH rule_id: blob_extract_03
- input: originator = "0" -> ambiguous. Could be null or system. Heuristic: if created_by_user_id == 0 and event_type in [sys_alert, cron_job] -> mapped_originator: "system" confidence: MEDIUM rule_id: originator_zero_heuristic
- input freeform_tags = "cust, retention;VIP [beta]" -> tokenize -> cust->customer via canonical table; retention -> retention; VIP beta -> tag:premium; flag:beta-user

Edge cases to explicitly flag for review:
- name collisions: "support" could be a role tag or a product name (support-tool). If row contains product_id -> prefer product.
- language-mixed tokens: e.g., "cliente, customer" duplicates in multilingual imports -> deduplicate after canonicalization.
- admin-intent strings like "do-not-process" or "test" -> map to special buckets and exclude from training.
- contradictory fields: metadata_blob.owner = "eng-ops" but created_by = "customer-service" -> keep both, add provenance priority (explicit owner field > created_by > inferred) and surface conflict to review pipeline.

Sample canonicalization table (starter):
- customer: ["cust", "customer", "client", "cliente", "custmer", "consumer"]
- system: ["system", "svc", "service", "sys"]
- partner: ["partner", "integrator", "3p", "third-party"]
- production: ["prod", "production", "live"]

Fuzzy rules (temporary):
- use Damerau-Levenshtein with threshold 1 for tokens length <= 6, threshold 2 for length 7-20.
- only accept fuzzy matches if token frequency in corpus > 50 occurrences OR token co-occurs 90%+ with a canonical token in the same row after stage1.

Sampling plan for human review (to seed better rules):
- stratified by rule_id=UNKNOWN, confidence=LOW: sample 200 rows
- all conflict rows (fields disagreeing on owner/source): sample 300 rows
- rare tokens (occurrence < 20): sample 500 rows (to catch typos and regional spellings)
- sample should preserve date distribution (older data has different patterns)

Quick regex snippets (to include in mapping engine):
- email-domain: /@([A-Za-z0-9.-]+)/?$/ -> group1
- prod api: /prod(?:uction)?[_-]?api/i
- numeric id: /(?:^|\D)(\d{5,})($|\D)/ -> captures long ids
- bracketed tags: /\[(.*?)\]/g -> iterate

Open questions / TODOs:
- How much history do we keep per-row? Snapshot every transformation or only latest? (lean towards incremental audit log per-row but storage/ETL cost)
- Storage schema for rule provenance: flat rule_id list? single rule_id? need to support multiple transforms per row. (implementation constraint in BigQuery partitions)
- Who signs off on canonical table additions? PM or labeling lead? propose weekly triage with eng + labeling.
- Should we expose an internal UI for quick adjudications? (low-effort MVP: spreadsheet export with prefilled mapping + two columns: keep/change + note)

Mini-adjudication script idea (ad-hoc for initial pass):
1) export low-confidence rows to sheet with columns [row_id, raw_value, suggested_mapping, confidence, rule_id, context_cols...]
2) reviewers tick checkbox: accept/reject and optionally type correction
3) ingest back via small CSV with manual_review = TRUE and override mappings applied; store reviewer name + timestamp

Notes to self / next steps:
- build canonical table as small JSON file shipped with transform code (easy to update), but persist changes and diff for audits.
- add unit tests with examples above (include typos + blob extraction cases)
- coordinate with infra: need streaming-light-weight transforms for live ingestion vs batch backfills (different rule sets?)
- tag this doc and drop into weekly label-squad sync for quick gut-checks

Random examples for test corpus (copy/paste friendly):
1) { row_id: 101, src: "Prod-API-v2", source_system: "", metadata_blob: "{"ingested_by":"partner-x"}", created_by: "42" } -> mapped_source: "partner-x" (since metadata_blob beats empty)
2) { row_id: 102, originator: "0", event_type: "cron_job", created_by_user_id: "0" } -> originator: "system"
3) { row_id: 203, freeform_tags: "beta; vip, cust" } -> tags: ["beta", "premium", "customer"]

Scratch checklist (very practical):
- [ ] finalize canonical table v0.1 and put in repo as "canonicalize.json"
- [ ] implement stage 1-3 transforms in labeling-utils (PR link above)
- [ ] add sample export for manual adjudication (sheet + import endpoint)
- [ ] decide retention policy for per-row audit trail
- [ ] follow up with infra re: BigQuery schema changes (ticket created: JIRA-LL-987)

If time: write short doc for CS/partner teams explaining how legacy source mapping might alter analytics (e.g., partner names merged, old partner aliases consolidated).

End of scratchpad.

(Keep as living doc — lots of TODOs. Remove sensitive partner names before share.)
